extracted.intended_audience: writers, editors, designers, and publishing professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A glossary of publishing, typography, and production terms that also contains practical guidelines and standards for preparing, formatting, and producing books, journals, and electronic publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition designation
rubrics_metrics.description: A publication in its original form, or any subsequent reissue of the publication in which its content is significantly revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The designation “second edition” should be applied only when content is significantly revised; it should not be applied to a secondary format (e.g., cloth vs. paperback) or to a second/subsequent impression in the absence of significant content changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect-binding design margin accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfect binding involves roughening the spine and applying adhesive so that part of the inside margin will be lost in the binding process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs for perfect-bound books should account for the fact that part of the inside margin will be lost; plan margins and type area accordingly to avoid text being trapped in the gutter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid widows and orphans
rubrics_metrics.description: Widow: a short paragraph-ending line at the top of a page. Orphan: the first line of a paragraph stranded at the bottom of a page or column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widows and orphans should be avoided when possible by changes in wording or spacing that either remove the line or lengthen it; use layout and copy edits to correct these situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image resolution standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution: the number of pixels per unit of measure used to form an image (pixels per inch) or the number of dots per unit of measure at which an image or page is output (dots per inch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the U.S., image and output resolution are calculated per inch; the more pixels/dots per inch, the higher the quality. Specify required ppi/dpi for images and output devices to ensure acceptable reproduction quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-scan considerations (scan/scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: When scanning an image, consider the resolution and the scaling percentage of the desired output before scanning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide final output size and required resolution up front so scans are made at an appropriate resolution and scale to avoid loss of quality or unnecessary large files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opacity as paper quality criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Opacity measures transparency of paper: the higher a paper’s opacity, the less tendency there is for text and images printed on one side to show through to the other side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select paper opacity appropriate to the publication to prevent show-through; higher opacity is required for double-sided printing when show-through would be distracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector graphics (SVG) preferred for web/mobile
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector graphic: an image defined by shapes rather than pixels. Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) is a standard defining vector graphics for XML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because SVG images are searchable and resolution independent, they are a preferred format for websites and mobile devices over bitmaps for line art and graphics that must scale cleanly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF for stable, device-independent delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: PDF (Portable Document Format) is a file format for stable, device-independent delivery of electronic documents, preserving fonts, layout, and pagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PDF to deliver files for final printing or stable electronic distribution; it preserves design intent across platforms and is appropriate for many journal articles, e-books, and print proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata content and syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata is data about data and may include copyright information, an ISBN or ISSN, a volume or issue number, the title and creator of the work, and a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record metadata using a standard syntax (often XML-based) and include the customary fields (copyright, identifiers, title/creator, description) to facilitate discovery, ordering, and inventory tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISBN per format
rubrics_metrics.description: ISBN (International Standard Book Number) is usually assigned to each book in each format (e.g., cloth, paperback, or e-book).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should assign an ISBN to each distinct format of a book to uniquely identify the product for ordering, distribution, and inventory systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISSN for serials and some monograph series
rubrics_metrics.description: ISSN (International Standard Serial Number) is an eight-digit number that identifies a titled journal or other periodical; books that are part of a monograph series may also be assigned an ISSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ISSNs for serial publications and consider ISSN assignment for monograph series in addition to ISBNs to aid identification in serials databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposition is the process of arranging pages so that, when folded, they will appear in the correct order, sequence, and orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure imposition reflects the final binding and folding scheme (and consider trim/creep) so pages appear in the intended order and orientation after printing and binding; use CTP/automation where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process color printing (CMYK) specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Process color printing reproduces full-color artwork using several plates (usually four) printing cyan, magenta, yellow, and black (CMYK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare full-color artwork with appropriate separations and halftone screening for CMYK process printing; expect color conversion from RGB and specify color management expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone screen fineness
rubrics_metrics.description: A halftone screen breaks a continuous-tone image into a pattern of dots; the fineness is denoted in lines per inch (e.g., a 133-line screen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select an appropriate screen frequency for the printing process and paper; finer screens yield more detail but may require higher quality paper and press control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepress and proof stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepress comprises the processes between receipt of electronic files and printing; a publication may involve several stages of proof (galley proof, page proof, color proof, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and allow for multiple proof rounds appropriate to the project (checks for text, pagination, color, and corrections). Use the correct proof type for the stage (galley vs. page vs. color proof) to catch relevant issues before press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain-text file definition for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A plain-text file contains only letters, numerals, punctuation, spaces, returns, line breaks, and tabs with no additional formatting or special characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting plain-text files, avoid special formatting and nonstandard encodings; specify encoding (e.g., UTF-8) if non-ASCII characters are required and prefer plain-text for machine-readable workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint use for time-sensitive dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprint: part of a work printed and distributed or posted online before publication to mitigate delay of publication schedules and peer review in time-sensitive fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preprints to disseminate findings promptly in time-sensitive disciplines, but be aware of journal policies and the status of peer review; label preprints clearly as not peer-reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kerning/letterspacing to improve readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Kerning is the selective adjustment of space between particular characters to improve appearance or ease of reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply kerning judiciously during typesetting to improve typographic color and legibility; excessive or inconsistent letterspacing can hinder readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure (line length) as design consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure: the length of the line (usually in picas) in which type is set; full measure is the full width of the type page, narrow measure is an indented or shortened block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an appropriate measure (line length) for legibility—avoid measures that are too long or too short for comfortable reading; adjust measure for multi-column makeup and special elements like long quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trim size and type page definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Trim size: the dimensions of a full page in a printed publication. Type page: the area occupied by the type image from running head to last line of type and from inside to outside margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify final trim size early; design the type page (margins, running heads, folios) within that trim so pagination, layout, and binding are correct for the chosen format.
